title: Negative Angles? Unit Circle Explained Simply | PUC Maths Class 11
description:
Ride a bicycle forward and the tyre valve goes round one way. Push it backwards and it goes round the other way. Both are turns, but not the same turn. How can one number say which way? In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 3, Trigonometric Functions) we set up the unit circle and measure angles on it.

You will see the unit circle drawn step by step, positive (anticlockwise) and negative (clockwise) angles side by side, the four quadrants, a ray turning past one full turn to 420°, and the real number line wrapped live around the circle so that every real number becomes an angle in radians. We prove in small steps that θ and 2nπ + θ end at the same point, turn -1000° in a worked example, fix the trap of thinking a difference of π gives the same point, and solve an original JEE Main pattern question. Two pause-and-think questions, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11 and JEE Main students.

In this video:

1:31 Quadrants and more than one turn
1:59 Live: wrap the number line around the circle
2:37 Proof: θ and 2nπ + θ end at the same point
3:33 Worked example: where does -1000° end?
4:18 Exam trap: a difference of π
4:35 Where it is asked
4:45 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:27 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 27): Definitions of Sine, Cosine and Other Trigonometric Functions. How high is the valve above the hub?
